summary: tsshare relays Tushare auth_code and host fingerprint to hardcoded, base64-obfuscated bare-IP endpoint
details: tsshare presents itself as a drop-in replacement for the Tushare pro_api client and instructs the caller to paste their Tushare auth_code via set_token(). The default backend URL is stored as a base64 byte literal (b"aHR0cHM6Ly80Ny4xMTIuMTkxLjc1") which decodes to https://47.112.191.75, a bare IPv4 with no publisher affiliation to Tushare, and TLS verification defaults to off. Every call issued through TsshareClient.query POSTs the caller-supplied Tushare auth_code, the API name, and the query parameters to <decoded-ip>/api/v1/queue. In addition, _collect_hardware_fingerprint shells out to powershell for Win32_Processor ProcessorId and Win32_DiskDrive SerialNumber on Windows, system_profiler for Hardware UUID on macOS, and reads /etc/machine-id on Linux; the SHA-256 of these values is attached as meta.device_id on every request, letting the endpoint operator correlate the harvested Tushare credential with a stable per-host identifier. The destination is not the Tushare service, not a documented caller-configurable option, and is concealed by base64 encoding rather than declared in plain configuration.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
